ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, D and C are the trisection points of arc BE, $\angle COD=32^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle E$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since D and C are the trisecting points of the arc BE,\\
thus, arc DE = arc CD = arc BC,\\
thus, $\angle$BOC = $\angle$COD = $\angle$DOE = $32^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle$BOE = $3 \times 32^\circ = 96^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle$A = $\frac{1}{2}\angle$BOE = $48^\circ$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{48^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, D and C are the trisection points of arc BE, and $\angle COD = 32^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle E$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O, AB is a horizontal diameter passing through the center O, A is at the left end, and B is at the right end. Points E, D, C are located on the arc of the upper half of the circle, and along the minor arc BE the order may be regarded as B, C, D, E; in the figure OE, OD, OC and chord AE are drawn, so the sought ∠E is the angle at point E in triangle AOE. Reasoning: D and C are the trisection points of arc BE, therefore arcs BC, CD, DE are equal. ∠COD is a central angle, corresponding to arc CD, and it is known that ∠COD = 32°, so the degree measure of each small arc BC, CD, DE is 32°. Thus the degree measure of minor arc BE is 32° × 3 = 96°, that is, the central angle ∠BOE = 96°. Because AB is a diameter, OA and OB are opposite rays, ∠AOE = 180° - 96° = 84°. In triangle AOE, OA = OE, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠OAE and ∠AEO are equal. Therefore ∠E = ∠AEO = (180° - 84°) / 2 = 48°.
